Search Change layout Close Add to quote Close Back To Plate Loaded Strength Training Equipment Catalog Home New Product Configure hammer strength Plate Loaded Pendulum-X Squat The Plate Loaded Pendulum-X Squat is built for athletes and serious lifters who demand more from their lower-body training. Unlike traditional pendulum squats that limit hip extension and overload the knees, the Pendulum-X drives total-body extension for unmatched power and performance. Its patent-pending movement dynamically shifts resistance—lighter at the bottom where you’re weakest and heavier at the top where you generate maximum force—creating the perfect strength curve for explosive results. Engineered for elite athletes, this machine builds stronger legs, powerful hips, and next-level performance. Dimensions (L x W x H): 97 x 45 x 81 in (246 x 114 x 206 cm) Weight: 804 lb (365 kg) View All Specs + Add to quote Plate Loaded Pendulum-X Squat Jump to a section Contact a Rep Now Key Feature Adjustable Foot Platform More Key Feature Range of Motion Adjustment More Key Feature Assisting Band Pegs More The X-Factor in Squatting The Pendulum-X Squat is engineered for total body extension. Traditional pendulum squats keep athletes in constant knee flexion, overloading the joints while limiting posterior chain activation and hip extension—both critical for athletic power. This movement changes the game by allowing a full, natural drive at the top, unlocking maximal force production for explosive jumps, sprints, and overall strength. It's not just about squatting deep; it's about training the way you compete. That’s the X-factor. Not Just New. Never Done Before. The Pendulum-X Squat isn’t just another pendulum squat—it’s a breakthrough in lower-body training. Our patent-pending resistance curve adjusts load throughout the lift, making it lighter at the bottom where athletes are weakest and heavier at the top where they generate the most force. This dynamic loading reinforces explosive strength, unlocking full hip extension for next-level athletic performance. When innovation meets intensity, results follow. Product Configurator Customize your own Pendulum-X Squat Customize your equipment like never before with our 3D configurator tool, featuring augmented reality to visualize and drop your design directly into your space. View in 3D View in 3D Specs Dimensions (L x W x H) 97 x 45 x 81 in (246 x 114 x 206 cm) Weight 804 lb (365 kg) Max Load Capacity (per arm) 4 x 45 lb plates (4 x 20 kg plates) Expand to see all specs Starting Resistance (per arm) 81 lb (37 kg) Product Code PL-XSQ Storage Weight Horns 6 Recommended Plate Mix 6 x 45 lb plates, 4 x 25 lb plates, 4 x 10 lb plates FAQ Why is full hip extension so important when squatting? Full hip extension is the final phase of explosive movements like sprinting, jumping, and Olympic lifting. Without it, you’re leaving strength and performance gains on the table. The Pendulum-X Squat ensures complete lower-body activation, maximizing quad, glute, and hamstring development in a way that translates directly to sport. Is the Hammer Strength Pendulum-X Squat easier on the knees than traditional pendulum squats? Yes. By eliminating constant knee flexion, the Pendulum-X Squat reduces shear stress and overuse on the knee joint. Instead of forcing the quads to take all the load, it distributes the resistance more effectively, making it ideal for athletes focused on longevity and performance. How does the Plate Loaded Pendulum-X Squat machine target the glutes? The Pendulum-X Squat is designed to maximize glute activation by promoting full hip extension at the top of the lift, which is essential for optimal glute recruitment. Unlike traditional pendulum squats that often limit hip extension, the patented movement of the Pendulum-X ensures that your glutes are fully engaged throughout the range of motion. How many racking positions on the Pendulum-X Squat machine are there and what is their spacing? There are 3 racking heights spaced 5 inches apart to accommodate athletes of all shapes and sizes. The entire gunrack can also be adjusted up or down to provide more adjustability based on your athletes and programs. Search Change layout Close Add to quote Close Back To Plate Loaded Strength Training Equipment Catalog Home New Product Configure hammer strength Plate Loaded Super Fly The Plate Loaded Super Fly isn’t your typical fly machine. Designed to push the boundaries of chest training, it offers both flat and decline fly positions, giving athletes the flexibility to target the chest from multiple angles for maximum muscle engagement. The multiple, flaring FreedomFly back pads allow the shoulders to move freely and deeper during each rep—without rubbing or restriction. Whether you’re chasing strength, endurance, or muscle definition, the Super Fly takes your chest workout to the next level, providing superior range of motion and optimized comfort for every press and fly movement. Dimensions (L x W x H): 82 x 86 x 41 in (208 x 218 x 104 cm) Weight: 306 lb (139 kg) View All Specs + Add to quote Plate Loaded Super Fly Jump to a section Contact a Rep Now Key Feature Flat-to-Decline Adjustment More Key Feature Extra-Long Handles More Key Feature FreedomFly Back Pads More More Than Just a Fly Fly machines haven’t changed in decades—until now. The Super Fly goes beyond the ordinary, offering both flat and decline positions so athletes can train at the angle that best fits their goals. This isn’t just another fly machine; it’s a new standard in plate-loaded chest training, built for those who demand more from every rep. Start Light. Load Heavy. With a light starting resistance of just 14 lbs per arm, the Super Fly is perfect for controlled, high-rep work or dialing in form. But when it’s time to load up, this machine is built to handle serious weight. Plus, the Range of Motion adjustment lets you go deeper for an even greater stretch and contraction, giving you total control over every rep. View in 3D View in 3D Specs Dimensions (L x W x H) 82 x 86 x 41 in (208 x 218 x 104 cm) Weight 306 lb (139 kg) Max Load Capacity (per arm) 3 x 45 lb plates (3 x 20 kg plates) Expand to see all specs Starting Resistance (per arm) 14 lb (6.3 kg) Product Code PL-FLY Storage Weight Horns 4 Recommended Plate Mix 4 x 45 lb plates, 2 x 25 lb plates, 2 x 10 lb plates FAQ Is there a range of motion adjustment on the Super Fly machine? If so, where is it located? Yes—the Hammer Strength Super Fly features a range of motion adjustment to control the depth of your fly stretch. This flip-on, flip-off mechanism is located just under each fly workarm where it rests on the bumper. What is the purpose of the raised foot placement location on the Plate Loaded Super Fly? The raised foot placement helps ensure proper alignment during the movement, preventing unnatural overextension and keeping the body in an optimal position during flys. By stabilizing the lower body, it allows athletes to focus on powerful, controlled reps without compensating through improper mechanics. Why add adjustability to a Hammer Strength fly machine? Traditional fly machines lock users into a single movement pattern, but no two athletes are built the same. The Super Fly machine’s adjustability—through its Flat-to-Decline positioning and Range of Motion adjustment—allows users to fine-tune the movement to their body mechanics, training goals, and mobility needs. This means better muscle activation, a more natural feel, and a fly that works with you, not against you. Can the athlete get a full squeeze at the top of the movement of the Super Fly? Absolutely. The Hammer Strength Super Fly is designed for complete pec contraction. With its extended range of motion and extra-long handles, you can achieve a full, powerful squeeze at the top of each rep. The FreedomFly Back Pads also allow your shoulders to move more freely, letting you drive the handles together without restriction—maximizing chest activation like never before. The Ground Base® Multi-Squat allows users to face either direction based on their training goals and comfort. Facing out provides a more traditional squat setup with a natural grip on the angled handles, while facing in can adjust the loading pattern and engagement. Both options reinforce full-body stability and proper force production. What grip options do the angled handles provide on the Hammer Strength Multi-Squat? The angled handles offer both high and low grip positions to accommodate different movements. Use the higher handles for squats and lunges to maintain an upright posture and controlled movement. The lower handles are ideal for deadlifts and hinge-based exercises, promoting a strong, athletic pull from the ground. What makes the Ground Base® Multi-Squat machine different from traditional free-weight squats? While the Ground Base® Multi-Squat still reinforces full-body stabilization and controlled force production, it allows for a more guided motion, whereas a traditional barbell squat is not guided. How does the Ground Base® Multi-Squat help with athletic performance? By reinforcing proper foot positioning, balance, and force production from the ground up, the Ground Base® Multi-Squat helps athletes build strength and coordination that directly translates to explosive power in sport movements. What is the difference between the top and low loading positions on the Multi-Squat? The top-loading position creates a more descending strength curve, meaning the resistance is highest at the beginning of the movement and gradually decreases as you reach the top. In contrast, the low-loading position generates a more ascending strength curve, where resistance is lighter at the start and increases as you complete the lift.
